question: In the EU strategy on combating antisemitism and fostering Jewish life, the Commission stated: ‘the adoption of the IHRA definition and the appointment of special envoys or coordinators by all Member States are also necessary steps for effective action at national level.’ 1.
What steps has the Commission taken to ensure that these measures are implemented by the Member States?
Which Member States have adopted the IHRA definition since the adoption of the strategy?
Which Member States have appointed special envoys or coordinators since the adoption of the strategy?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.4.2024) The Commission adopted on 5 October 2021 the EU Strategy on combating antisemitism and fostering Jewish life.

The Member States endorsed the strategy in the Council Conclusions on combating racism and antisemitism, adopted on 4 March 2022, in which they committed to develop national strategies on combating antisemitism by end 2022, or include measures in their national action plans against racism.

As part of the implementation of the EU Strategy, the Commission expects and supports the development and implementation of national strategies, the adoption of the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance’s (IHRA) definition and the appointment of special envoys, through a Working Group that meets biannually, bringing together representatives from Member States and Jewish communities, most recently on 23-24 January 2024.

As of February 2024, 24 Member States1 have adopted or endorsed the IHRA definition, and 16 Member States2 have appointed a special envoy or national coordinator on combating antisemitism. The Commission will publish in the first half of 2024 a progress report on the EU Strategy that will include the monitoring of progress made at national level.
1 Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany,

Greece, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain and Sweden. 2 Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Germany, Greece, France, Hungary, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Portugal, Romania, and Spain.
